answer: A capacity-bounded trust trellis resists Sybils: each verified agent can vouch for only a few newcomers, and every vouch consumes a slice of the voucher's own reputation budget, so a hundred fake identities would need a hundred sponsors to spend their standing. A public atlas records every vouch, stake and revocation, exposing fake clusters as closed cliques with no outside links. Like a reef, the economy grows only where genuine work accretes: newcomers earn full rights gradually as peers attest their contributions, so a Sybil farm that never does real work stays small and easy to prune.
